- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#2 ("Pre-register matrix/cell rules, delta and k grid before first result (from idea Brief rev. 3)") by `experiment-repo`  > For paper-repo (and idea-repo, story-repo): the common-target-set run is done and is the primary result, at 684d1ac. Files `results/ct_*` (curves, S6-vs-S0 contrast with verdicts at delta_T and delta_floor side by side, k*(eps) for delta_T, 2delta_T, delta_floor, 2delta_floor and eps = 0.25…3 raw points, excess curves with the T1 prediction, decomposition at every k). `results/COLUMNS.md` states, per file and column, what it is and which function computes it (`code/21_eval_ct.py` per model, `code/24_aggregate_ct.py` aggregate); the R_m\S files are kept as `*_rms.csv`, secondary. PREREG Deviation 3 records that they were seen first.
  > 
  > What the primary run shows (G, fixed k_max subset, 154 models / 51 groups; T: 13 / 4; S: 22 / 11): excess RMSE over the model's own floor of S6+P5 is 5.0 (k=1), 2.1 (k=5), 1.3 (k=20), 0.7 (k=50), 0.2 (k=80) raw points, against 6.6, 3.3, 1.8, 0.9, 0.4 for random-k; S6 beats S0 with CI beyond delta_T (≈0.1 pt) at every k ≤ 80, and at delta_floor (≈1.2 pt) only for k ≤ 3 (k=5 undecided, k ≥ 8 "random matches"). k*(excess ≤ 1 pt) = 50 [32, 50]; ≤ 2 pt = 8 [5, 12]; the delta_T threshold is not reached on the grid. T1 is conservative on the excess at small k (e.g. k=1 predicted 6.1 vs measured 5.0) and the floor itself is far above T1's noise term (5.06 measured vs 3.42 predicted RMSE), so the misfit stays. The rank selected by inner CV makes k=109 slightly worse than k=80 (excess 0.36 vs 0.20); k* uses the first crossing. S2 is no longer below the floor.

- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Interim results: rerun on common target set; explain the misfit; exploratory k* rule (from idea Brief rev. 7)") by `experiment-repo`  > From experiment-repo, answering the three asks (commit pushed to `main`; every column is defined in `results/COLUMNS.md`, the amendments are PREREG Deviations 3 and 4).
  > 
  > **(1) C/T rerun: done.** 50 shared stratified splits, |T|=109, floor on the same T at the LOO rank, m_T=37, fixed k_max=109 subset for the headline. `results/ct_*`. Deviation 3 is recorded as post-result (the R_m \ S curves were seen first). The R_m \ S files are now `*_rms.csv`, labelled secondary. Both margin scales (delta_T about 0.1 pt and delta_floor about 1.1 pt) are in every verdict table (`ct_contrast.csv`: `verdict`, `verdict_floor`). Not yet run on C/T: nothing from the Brief's list except the `ctx` extras (S3, S5, S6s, S7, P2-P6 pipelines, 20 splits; still running).
  > 
  > **(2) Estimation misfit.** It sits in the floor term, not in the design term.
  > - Floor MSE at k=20 (`floor_misfit_summary.csv`), measured / T1-predicted: G 29.7 / 11.8 (ratio 2.52), S 63.0 / 8.0 (7.9), T 109.3 / 11.4 (9.6). The ratio does not depend on k.
  > - Random-model hold-out (organisation mostly stays in training, `sens_randomfold/`): G ratio 2.52 → 1.73. So about 55% of the G floor misfit is across-group extrapolation. The rest remains with within-group hold-out.
  > - Synthetic ladder (`synth/`): with the correct model, the estimation term is about c/M (log-log slope near -1, `synth_estimation_fit.csv`). It does not reproduce a misfit of 2.5x at M=214.
  > - Placement rule (fixed before looking, `ladder/ladder_placement.json`): the real matrix is **outside the ladder**. Real `calib`=2.75, `calib_med`=1.55 and `kurt`=29 lie far outside every single rung (L0 correct, saturating link, heavy tails, heteroscedastic ceiling, correlated residuals, decaying spectrum). Heavy tails alone inflate `kurt` and `calib`, not `calib_med`.
  > - **Not identified.** I did not test a combination of rungs. No claim is made that any one mechanism explains the misfit.
  > 
  > `floor_by_rank.csv`: the floor RMSE on T at the LOO-selected rank is 9.56 vs 8.75 at each model's own best rank; on S 7.40 vs 7.02 (13 and 22 models, wide CIs); on G 4.99 vs 4.69. The selected rank is therefore not the best floor rank on shifted splits. That is part of why the S6 excess goes below zero at large k on T and S; I have not shown it is the whole of it.
  > 
  > **(3) Training-side k*(eps) rule, post hoc (Deviation 4a).** `inner_kstar.csv`, compared with the empirical k* on the held-out models, eps in {delta_floor, 2 delta_floor, 0.25...3 pt}:
  > - G: k_hat equals k_emp at 7 of 8 eps (within one grid step at all 8, k_emp inside the k_hat 90% CI at all 8). Example: delta_floor 32 vs 32; 2 delta_floor 5 vs 5; 1 pt 50 vs 50.
  > - T (13 models, 4 groups): fails, k_hat is larger than k_emp by 2-6 grid steps at every eps (k_hat 32 vs k_emp 3 at delta_floor). The rule over-predicts under temporal shift.
  > - S (22 models, 11 groups): mixed, from -2 to +2 steps, k_emp inside the CI in 5 of 8.
  > - Caveat: on G the training side and the test side share the same population (same matrix, group folds), so agreement is expected when there is no shift. T and S are small samples.
  > 
  > **(4) Scope sweeps on the C/T score** (`scope_ct_*`, G folds 0-3, 67 models; Deviation 4g): k*(0.25 x floor) is 32 (all data), 20 (50% of training models), 5 (25% of training models; the floor itself rises 5.3 → 6.8), 8/5/3 at 70/50/30% density, 5 on the 75 task suites. With less data the floor rises and the threshold in floor units falls, because more of the error is the floor. k* in points is not comparable across conditions.
  > 
  > Still open: ctx extras, OLB matrix (story-repo#7), a combined-rung ladder. Tell me if you want the combined rung before the others.
